papers.title: Cascading Contingency Analysis of Modern Power Systems Using a Stochastic Hybrid Systems Framework
papers.summary: This paper presents a cascading contingency analysis and risk assessment framework that incorporates probabilistic mode transitions motivated by stochastic hybrid system (SHS) concepts together with power-flow-based stress evaluation. A two-stage modeling approach is adopted in which sensitivity-based analysis is first used to identify candidate cascading transitions, followed by DC power flow re-evaluation to accurately capture post-contingency stress redistribution, islanding behavior, and load shedding. A probabilistic propagation model is constructed using mode-dependent transition probabilities derived from line loading conditions. A Cascading Risk Index (CRI) is introduced to quantify the expected load shedding accumulated over cascade progression. Case studies on the IEEE 39-bus system demonstrate that the proposed framework captures diverse cascading routes under multiple initiating outages and identifies critical propagation patterns that are not revealed by N-1/N-2 screening. The results highlight the importance of SHS modeling in assessing cascading risk and providing a scalable framework for resilience evaluation in modern power systems.

papers.title: Analysis and Demonstration of a Current-Stiff, Isolated Capacitive Bridge Transformer
papers.summary: The traditional Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) based Dual Active Bridge (DAB) utilizes a transformer at its center to provide galvanic isolation and a turns ratio for step up/down functionality. However, the transformer is often the limiting factor of the DAB, especially as semiconductor switching speeds improve, given steel core losses, winding losses, etc. This paper presents a new DAB architecture based on Current Source Inverters (CSIs) coupled through, and isolated by, an AC capacitive bridge, yielding a system called a Capacitive Bridge Transformer (CBT). The CBT architecture eliminates all magnetic components in the AC portion of the isolated DAB circuit, reducing frequency scaling barriers normally present in DABs. The paper introduces the CBT from the perspective of duality and then develops the DC-DC power flow equations, the internal apparent power equations, and effective turns ratio. The analytical models are verified by steady state and detailed time domain measurements on a 2 kW experimental prototype.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Offline Reinforcement Learning with Online Action Selection Enabled by Sparse Gaussian-Process Critics
papers.summary: Start-ups and grade changes remain largely operator-driven, while developing and maintaining dynamic models for model-based control requires substantial engineering effort. Hybrid Offline Learning and Online Optimisation (HOFLON) uses one-step offline reinforcement learning to select actions from historical transition data. In its original implementation, the online objective combines the predicted return from a tree-ensemble critic with an adversarial-autoencoder (AAE) penalty for unfamiliar state-action pairs. We examine the effect of this penalty and replace the critic and AAE with a sparse variational Gaussian-process (sGP) critic. Actions maximise $μ- κσ$, an uncertainty-adjusted estimate of the return from one action followed by the historical operating practice. On the HOFLON polymerisation-reactor benchmark, removing the AAE from HOFLON led to 4 failed start-ups in 15 runs over five critics. At its published weight, the variation in the AAE penalty is four orders of magnitude smaller than the variation in the tree-ensemble critic. Nevertheless, it changes actions when the predicted returns of competing candidates are nearly equal, and paired runs with and without the penalty diverged from the first move. With a Matérn-5/2 sGP critic, $κ= 0$ led to failure in 13 of 15 runs, whereas with $κ= 3$ none of 15 runs (five critics, three noise realisations) failed. The median and lowest returns were 13,464 and 13,398 (HOFLON: 13,393 and 12,411). A squared-exponential sGP critic with learned inducing inputs needed $κ\geq 3$ to remain within the empirical data support in steady state, and then settled with a temperature offset of 2.0 K.

papers.title: Reliable and explainable analysis of AVS/RS by Statistical Model Checking and Process Mining
papers.summary: Automated Vehicle Storage and Retrieval Systems (AVS/RS) are increasingly adopted to boost warehouse throughput while containing operational costs. We present an integrated analysis framework that couples discrete-event simulation with Statistical Model Checking (SMC) and Process Mining (PM) to quantify and explain AVS/RS performance. SMC, implemented through the MultiVeStA tool, delivers statistically reliable estimates of key indicators, such as cycle times, throughput, and storage utilization, across alternative stocking and picking policies with user-specified confidence levels. MultiVeStA orchestrates multiple independent simulations in a black-box manner, enabling automated verification. PM ingests the resulting event logs to uncover the behavioral patterns and bottlenecks that drive those indicators, closing the interpretability gap typical of simulation studies. We instantiate the framework on a new open-source AVS/RS simulator configured according to recent industrial guidelines and evaluate multiple control strategies. Results show that the joint use of SMC and PM enables both predictive what-if analyses and post-hoc diagnostics, providing the first combined SMC+PM assessment of AVS/RS operations and a reusable toolchain for automated warehousing research.

papers.title: Energy- and Time-Efficient Multi-Vehicle Trajectory Planning Using Augmented DAG Search in Configuration Space
papers.summary: Multi-vehicle trajectory planning for CAV requires balancing energy consumption and travel time while ensuring safety and scalability. While travel-time-optimal methods based on Integer Programming exhibit poor scalability in large-scale multi-vehicle scenarios, existing energy-oriented approaches fail to balance energy consumption and travel time. We extend a configuration-space framework for multi-vehicle trajectory planning to jointly locally optimize travel time and energy consumption. A weighted energy-travel time objective is combined with an efficient augmented DAG search on two-dimensional decompositions of a high-dimensional configuration space, enabling scalable and collision-free coordination of large numbers of vehicles. Although the proposed framework is applicable to other traffic scenarios, such as roundabouts and vehicle-following, we focus on intersections as a representative and challenging planning problem. To further improve performance for our methodology, we also extend the method with an insertion-ordering heuristic that exploits reduced-space geometric information. Combined with nonlinear model predictive control, the proposed framework is shown to scale to 40 vehicles, outperform MILP-based and convex optimization baselines in dense intersections, and reduce energy consumption at equalized travel times relative to time-optimal planning.

papers.title: Concentration-Based Probabilistic Reachability for Linear Systems under Multiplicative Uncertainty and Additive Noise
papers.summary: This paper investigates probabilistic reachability for discrete-time linear stochastic systems subject to bounded multiplicative uncertainty and potentially unbounded additive noise. To address the conservatism of reachable sets constructed solely from covariance information, we develop two complementary approaches based on sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential matrix moment-generating-function characterizations. The sub-Gaussian approach relies on a worst-case envelope over the uncertainty support, whereas the sub-exponential approach exploits expectation-based propagation of the matrix variance proxy. Both approaches are used to construct probabilistic reachable sets with explicit probability guarantees, considering ellipsoidal confidence regions and half-space bounds. For the latter, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition under which the sub-exponential chance-constraint margin is no larger than its sub-Gaussian counterpart. Numerical results show that the proposed bounds can be less conservative than those based on the covariance, and illustrate the complementary nature of the two approaches across probability levels.

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Threshold Design for Sparse Event Encoding in Learning Systems
papers.summary: One approach to event-driven learning is to encode continuous signals as sparse events generated when signal changes exceed a prescribed threshold. However, this threshold is typically selected empirically, with limited theoretical guidance. This paper establishes a connection between threshold-based event encoding and discretized learning systems and identifies a dimensionless ratio governing information retention. From this connection, we derive an information-sufficiency boundary using normal-condition data and formulate a data-driven criterion that selects the sparsest threshold retaining a prescribed fraction of peak discriminative information. The framework is illustrated using event cameras and evaluated on power-system fault classification. Results show that the proposed design identifies sparse operating thresholds while exposing the tradeoff between information retention, event activity, and classification performance.

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: Physics-Informed Evaluation of ANN-based Power Flow Solvers under System Shift
papers.summary: Recent advances in artificial deep learning-based power flow (PF) solvers have primarily focused on improving estimation accuracy, while their physical feasibility and operational reliability under realistic system variations remain insufficiently evaluated. This paper proposes a physics-informed evaluation framework for deep learning-based PF solvers under topology and load distribution shifts. Beyond conventional voltage-domain errors, the framework incorporates KCL gaps, branch-flow gaps, KVL residuals, continuous feasibility scores, and strict, practical, and relaxed PF feasibility rates. Four case studies are designed to investigate topology shifts, mixed topology training, load distribution shifts, and combined topology distribution shifts. Eight ANN architectures, including graph input models, load-only baselines, and physics-informed neural networks, are evaluated under consistent settings. The results demonstrate that low estimation errors do not necessarily correspond to physically feasible or operationally reliable PF solutions, particularly under combined system shifts. The proposed framework establishes an initial foundation and analysis for the development and verification of trustworthy deep learning-based PF solvers, providing support for their reliable deployment in future AI-enabled power system analysis.
category_names_zh: eess.SY (系统与控制理论 (Systems and Control))

papers.title: Intelligent Carbon Emission-aware Radio Unit Activation Control in Dense Heterogeneous Energy 6G Networks
papers.summary: Base stations account for a dominant share of energy consumption and operational carbon emissions in radio access networks. In O-RAN deployments with heterogeneous energy sources, however, minimizing energy consumption alone does not necessarily minimize carbon emissions. In this work, we investigate carbon-aware DRL for RU sleep control. Under the adopted source-matched operational accounting model, renewable-matched RUs are assigned zero direct operational emissions, whereas non-renewable-supplied RUs incur operational emissions. The problem is formulated as a Markov decision process and evaluated using two carbon-aware reward formulations and a conventional energy--QoS reward baseline. We implement and compare TD3, PPO, and a heuristic method under realistic mobility and 3GPP channel models across multiple renewable-matched RU layouts and traffic loads. Simulation results show that TD3 learns more energy-efficient activation policies than PPO, achieving approximately 3%--6% lower energy consumption in representative scenarios. TD3 also achieves 8%--12% lower operational emissions than PPO in scenarios with a low proportion of renewable-matched RUs and up to a 20% reduction relative to the heuristic baseline under moderate renewable availability and high traffic load. Moreover, the joint energy,carbon and QoS reward achieves approximately 12%--28% lower operational emissions than the energy and QoS reward, while maintaining comparable energy consumption.
category_names_zh: eess.SY (系统与控制理论 (Systems and Control))

papers.title: Koopman Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: We propose a Koopman model-based reinforcement learning (K-MBRL) algorithm for controlling nonlinear robotic systems with unknown dynamics. The K-MBRL learns a control policy by minimizing an approximate policy objective that combines the analytical immediate cost with an estimate of the future cost evaluated at the one-step predicted state. To this end, we develop a stochastic Koopman operator-based learning method to approximate the unknown nonlinear dynamics in a linear representation, while a critic function estimates the remaining future cost. This formulation offers two key advantages. First, the linear Koopman dynamics simplify the model-dependent policy gradient computation to a constant matrix product, enabling computationally efficient policy improvement. Second, one-step model propagation mitigates the accumulation of prediction errors associated with long-horizon rollouts while retaining long-term cost information through the critic. The learned policy enables real-time control through feedforward evaluation without online optimization. We establish policy learning convergence guarantees under standard stochastic approximation assumptions. Simulations on HalfCheetah and quadruped four-legged locomotion tasks demonstrate strong sample efficiency and improved performance compared with classical model-free and model-based reinforcement learning baselines. A pendulum swing-up task is used to assess policy gradient approximation accuracy and conduct ablation studies on the learning mechanism and key hyperparameters. The proposed K-MBRL is further validated on a physical quadruped robot performing a challenging sequence of maneuvers: rising to an upright posture supported by two rounded rear feet, maintaining balance during bipedal walking, and safely returning to the ground, as shown in Fig.1.

papers.title: Discrete-Time Stochastic Control Beyond i.i.d. Noise
papers.summary: We study discrete-time stochastic control problems where the noise driving the state dynamics is a stationary infinite-order chain rather than an i.i.d. sequence. We formulate the problem as a controlled Markov process by enlarging the state space to include the posterior distribution of the noise given the state-action history. Assuming that the sensitivity of the noise transition kernel to past noise values decays exponentially, we show that the expected total variation distance between the full-history and finite-memory noise filters decays at rate $\sqrt{N}ρ^{\sqrt{N}}$. We use this result to construct finite-memory control models and establish explicit near-optimality bounds for their policies. Finally, under suitable ergodicity conditions, we show that Q-learning converges to the optimal solution of the approximate model, so the same performance bounds apply to the learned policies.

papers.title: Safe and Scalable Minimax Adaptive Control of Positive Systems
papers.summary: This paper studies minimax adaptive control of positive linear systems with fixed unknown dynamics and nonnegative disturbances. We reformulate the problem by compressing the historical data into a vector and a positivity-induced consistency set containing the models compatible with the observations. Together with the physical state, these quantities form a sufficient information state and yield an exact reformulation as a standard minimax dynamic game. We allow the admissible input set to adapt to the current consistency set, ensuring positivity for every remaining feasible model. As inconsistent models are eliminated, the input set can expand, allowing less cautious control actions. For finite model sets, we derive an explicit solution to the Bellman inequality and construct a safe and stabilizing certainty-equivalence controller with robustness guarantees. The framework also accommodates structured classes of continuum model uncertainty whose consistency sets admit fixed, finite-dimensional representations, enabling scalable information-state updates.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Indirect-Feedback Stochastic MPC with Gelbrich Ambiguity Sets
papers.summary: Stochastic model predictive control uses disturbance statistics to set safety margins. Errors in these statistics can invalidate the safety guarantees. This paper therefore describes the uncertainty in the disturbance mean and covariance by a prescribed Gelbrich ambiguity set. This contains distributions of any shape whose moments are close in the Gelbrich distance to the nominal values, including distributions with unbounded support. For linear time-invariant systems with additive disturbances, we build on the indirect feedback paradigm, propagate this moment uncertainty along the error dynamics, and obtain a closed-form constraint tightening that is computed offline. Robustness enters as a single additive term that grows with the size of the ambiguity set, so the online problem remains a quadratic program. Recursive feasibility and closed-loop satisfaction of conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraints hold for every disturbance distribution in the set. We illustrate the method on a linearized planar quadrotor.

papers.title: Excitable Behaviours of a First-Order High-Pass Neuron Model
papers.summary: With the rise of neuromorphic technologies, simple and tunable neuron models are needed to analyse and design spiking systems. However, the simplest neuron models, e.g., Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) models, usually fail to capture the excitable behaviours of biological neurons. This could be a significant limitation, as excitability enables reliable spike timing under parametric uncertainties. Recently, a minimal excitable model, the so-called High-Pass Model (HPM), was introduced in neuroengineering. It simply consists of a static sigmoid with a high-pass filter in positive feedback. Given its novelty, it is still unclear how easily the HPM can be tuned, and how much of the excitable behaviours of a biophysical neuron it can reproduce. To address these questions, we investigate the tunability of a first-order HPM sub- and supra-rheobase, i.e., below and above the onset of the tonic spiking regime (where the neuron spikes periodically), and compare its behaviours with those of a simple Hodgkin-Huxley-type Conductance-Based Model (CBM). Below rheobase, both models fire spikes in response to transient inputs, including post-inhibitory rebound spikes. Above rheobase, an affine reparametrization of the input of the HPM suffices to fit its frequency-current curve to that of a CBM. The two models mostly differ near their respective rheobases, where the first-order HPM lacks bistability and spike latency. We suggest that modifying the frequency-selective element of the HPM may be sufficient to overcome this limitation. These results highlight the potential of the HPM as a fundamental computational primitive in neuromorphic, spike-based technologies.
category_names_zh: eess.SY (系统与控制理论 (Systems and Control))

papers.title: Safety and Connectivity Certificates for Finite-Time Formation Transitions
papers.summary: Finite-time formation transitions are useful for coordinating multi-agent systems in time-critical missions, but convergence to a prescribed formation in finite time does not guarantee collision avoidance or communication connectivity during the transition. Existing approaches address finite-time coordination and safety-constrained formation control, yet explicit connections between disagreement during transitions, formation geometry, and coupling-gain selection need to be developed for certifying safe maneuvers. This paper develops a disagreement-based framework for certifying transient safety and connectivity during finite-time tracking of arbitrary prescribed formation trajectories. Local feedback guarantees exact finite-time tracking with a graph-independent settling-time bound, while a graph-dependent disagreement bound is used to derive sufficient geometric conditions for collision avoidance and connectivity preservation. These conditions further yield an offline coupling-gain selection rule based on the available geometric clearance. Numerical simulations illustrate the trade-off between convergence rate and control effort as the coupling gain increases. They also demonstrate the effectiveness and conservatism of the proposed certificates.
category_names_zh: eess.SY (系统与控制理论 (Systems and Control))
cs.MA (多智能体系统 (Multiagent))

papers.title: Online Adaptive Clustering in Robust Distributed Model Predictive Control
papers.summary: This paper proposes a dynamic clustering framework for tube-based model predictive control (MPC) of coupled multi-agent systems. Agents within a cluster coordinate their dynamics explicitly, while couplings from agents outside the cluster are treated as bounded disturbances. For each admissible cluster, we construct a state-dependent mismatch measure from a robust upper bound on its predicted closed-loop cost and an optimistic, partition-independent lower bound. Combining this mismatch with a communication penalty enables online selection of the clustering topology, ranging from centralized to fully decentralized operation. The resulting switching controller is shown to preserve recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction, and to render the closed-loop system practically asymptotically stable. Furthermore, the mismatch provides an upper bound on the finite-horizon performance difference with respect to centralized MPC. An eight-agent spring--damper example illustrates how the controller adapts cooperation while maintaining performance close to centralized MPC with reduced communication.
category_names_zh: eess.SY (系统与控制理论 (Systems and Control))

papers.title: The Role of Insurance in Power-System Risk Management: A Critical Review
papers.summary: Modern power systems are becoming more renewable-rich, digitalized, and interconnected, making risk propagation and economic consequences increasingly complex. Physical mitigation remains the primary means of risk control, but technical and economic limits leave residual risk. Insurance can complement these measures by transferring associated economic losses and influencing power-system decisions through risk-responsive terms. Despite growing interest, the literature remains fragmented across power-system engineering, actuarial science, and risk finance. This review develops an integrated physical-financial perspective for reviewing insurance in power systems. It examines how power system risks generate residual economic losses and the conditions under which these losses can be insured and transferred. It then develops an actuarial framework for insured-loss assessment and pricing. Insurance-aware decision-making is synthesized through four coupling levels describing how financial protection interacts with power-system decisions. Further progress is constrained by weak physical-financial loss validation, incomplete representation of systemic and evolving portfolio risk, and limited empirical and actuarial grounding of insurance-decision feedback. Research priorities include stronger physical-financial data linkage, forward-looking portfolio assessment, multi-timescale decision feedback, and empirical validation. Addressing these priorities would help move power-system insurance from fragmented applications toward a more coherent approach to residual-risk management in future power systems.
category_names_zh: math.OC (运筹学、优化与控制论)

papers.title: Towards Mode-Balanced Intersection Control: Hierarchical Coordination of Signal Timings, AV Trajectories, and Cyclist Speed Advice
papers.summary: Connected and automated vehicles (AVs) enable traffic signals and vehicle trajectories to be optimised jointly, but existing co-optimisation frameworks overlook cyclists, even though they share the same intersections. We propose a hierarchical framework that optimises traffic signal timings, AV trajectories, and cyclist speed advice to reduce travel times for both motorised vehicles and cyclists. The upper level jointly optimises signal timings and cyclist speed advice, while the lower level optimises AV trajectories and also updates cyclist speed advice obtained from the higher level at a higher frequency based on the resulting signal plan. The framework is evaluated in simulation under multiple demand profiles and optimisation parameter settings. Compared with optimized vehicle trajectories with fixed-time signal control, the proposed framework reduces mean travel times by 13.6\% for AVs and 12.3\% for cyclists. Adding cyclist speed advice further reduces mean cyclist waiting time by about 80\% relative to the same framework without speed advice. These results demonstrate substantial benefits for both modes of transport.
category_names_zh: eess.SY (系统与控制理论 (Systems and Control))

papers.title: Towards Design of Efficient Neuromorphic Controllers
papers.summary: One of the major sources of inspiration for neuromorphic engineering is the central nervous system, which is orders of magnitude more efficient than classical digital clock-based computers. Neuromorphic control aims at recreating this efficiency in control systems, combined with (formal) stability and performance guarantees. In our previous work [1], we have established formal guarantees for the emulation of static output feedback controllers implemented using integrate-and-fire neurons. In this paper, we investigate the ``efficiency'' of the resulting controllers in terms of sparse spiking activity. By changing the network structure of our original implementation, foregoing the unit gain assumption made in our previous work, we will establish that the chosen architecture of the spiking controller significantly affects its sparsity and discuss the implications of these observations for the efficient implementation of spiking controllers.
category_names_zh: eess.SY (系统与控制理论 (Systems and Control))

papers.title: Learn-To-Propagate: Distributionally Robust Motion Planning for Nonlinear Uncertain Systems
papers.summary: Motion planning for stochastic systems aims to find a sequence of control inputs that drives a system to a goal set while avoiding unsafe states with high probability. Existing approaches, however, are either restricted to linear dynamics with perfect knowledge of the underlying distributions or lack formal correctness guarantees. To address these limitations, we propose \emph{Learn-To-Propagate Distributionally-Robust Forest (L2P-DR-Forest)}, a distributionally-robust sampling-based planning algorithm for \emph{nonlinear} stochastic systems with \emph{unknown} initial state and process noise distributions. Our approach leverages recent advances in optimal transport to learn ambiguity sets that contain the true system distributions with high confidence. We develop an efficient method for propagating these sets through the system dynamics and for verifying their safety. We then integrate these techniques into a novel sampling-based planning algorithm to grow a forest of search trees in the system's state space while accounting for and mitigating the growth of ambiguity-sets radii. We prove that the algorithm is correct, i.e., every returned plan satisfies the specifications with the prescribed confidence, and, under some feasibility and distributional assumptions, is probabilistically complete. Evaluations on several robotic benchmarks demonstrate that our algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods while providing formal guarantees with high confidence.
category_names_zh: cs.RO (机器人学与具身智能)
eess.SY (系统与控制理论 (Systems and Control))

papers.title: Optimal Last-Iterate Bounds for Nonexpansive Stochastic Approximation
papers.summary: We establish last-iterate mean-square residual bounds for nonexpansive stochastic approximation (SA), or stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann (KM) iterations. In particular, we consider fixed-point mappings that are nonexpansive with respect to the Euclidean norm, and focus on polynomially decaying stepsizes. We study three conditions on the conditional second moment of the noise, and obtain bounds that are optimal up to logarithmic factors in each case. When it scales linearly with the squared residual, the best rate is $O(1/k^{1-ε})$ for any $ε>0$. In this case, for all considered stepsizes, our bounds match those of the noiseless KM iteration. When it is bounded by a constant, the best rate is $O(\log^2 k/\sqrt{k})$. When it scales affinely with the squared norm of the iterate, the best rate is $O(1/k^{1/2-ε})$, and the mean-square residual can diverge if the stepsizes are not square-summable. Thus, unlike for contractive SA, square-summable stepsizes are necessary for nonexpansive SA. We demonstrate how various algorithms with cocoercive maps, such as stochastic gradient descent, linear SA, and learning in cocoercive games, fit into our framework, and how the different noise conditions arise in each of them.

papers.title: Event-based analysis of neuromorphic feedback systems
papers.summary: This article investigates the existence and stability of periodic behavior arising in the feedback interconnection of neuromorphic systems, which evolve according to continuous dynamics but interact only through discrete events. Exploiting the event-driven nature of this interaction, each system is modeled by an operator that maps the history of events to the delay of its response. Building on the fading-memory properties of these operators, the article develops a small-gain result establishing the existence, uniqueness, and robustness of periodic one-to-one rhythms.
category_names_zh: eess.SY (系统与控制理论 (Systems and Control))

papers.title: Neuromodulation Through Intrinsic Noise
papers.summary: Neuromodulation, the modulation of excitability through the regulation of neuronal parameters, is a key tool in neuromorphic control design. This paper investigates how spiking excitability can be modulated by intrinsic noise. Focusing on a simplified memristive neuron model, we show that intrinsic noise plays distinct functional roles depending on the feedback pathways: Intrinsic noise in the fast excitatory feedback shapes the nature of excitability and modulates the sensitivity of the neuron to external/internal stimuli, whereas that in the slow inhibitory feedback provides internal stimuli that can trigger stochastic spiking. We expect these findings to guide the design of neuromorphic systems that harness intrinsic noise to exploit beneficial stochastic phenomena, such as stochastic resonance.
category_names_zh: q-bio.NC (神经科学与脑认知)
eess.SY (系统与控制理论 (Systems and Control))

papers.title: FAME-QP: A GPU-Accelerated Quadratic-Programming Solver for Real-Time Model Predictive Control
papers.summary: We present FAME-QP, a GPU-accelerated solver for dense quadratic programs arising in linear model predictive control. FAME-QP combines constraint-dependent operator representations with fused single- and two-kernel iterations replayed through CUDA graphs, automatically selecting the execution configuration through device calibration and problem-specific timing. It probes a cached operator bank to select the initial penalty and updates operators lazily when problem matrices change. Numerical benchmarks and simulated humanoid and quadrotor control experiments demonstrate reduced latency relative to competing GPU solvers while maintaining solution accuracy and control performance.
category_names_zh: cs.RO (机器人学与具身智能)
cs.GR (计算机图形学)
eess.SY (系统与控制理论 (Systems and Control))

papers.title: Continuous-Time Modeling of Destination-Constrained Dynamic Systems via Doob's $h$-Transform
papers.summary: Existing work on modeling destination-constrained dynamic systems has mainly focused on discrete-time formulations with linear destination constraints or Gaussian destination distributions. Since practical systems are more naturally modeled in continuous time and often subject to nonlinear/non-Gaussian constraints/distributions, this paper proposes a unified measure-transformation framework for continuous-time modeling of systems subject to deterministic or distributional constraints on a nonlinear function of the terminal state. The framework starts from an unconstrained Itô stochastic differential equation, typically derived from physical laws to describe the system's forward evolution without destination information, and takes its induced path measure as unconstrained measure. Doob's $h$-transform is employed to transform this measure into a constrained path measure incorporating destination information through an injected drift. The resulting system is proved to satisfy the constraints while preserving the laws of the unconstrained state process conditioned on the destination information. The transition density is derived, and the path measure of the distributionally constrained system is proved to uniquely minimize Kullback--Leibler divergence from the unconstrained path measure among those satisfying the same distributional constraint. Its injected drift is further shown to converge pointwise to that of the deterministically constrained system as the destination distribution shrinks to the prespecified value. For linear time-varying unconstrained systems, a simplified form of the constrained systems is derived in terms of the conditional expectation of the terminal state, leading to the development of trajectory-generation algorithms. Numerical simulations evaluate the proposed framework under both types of destination constraints.
